anomalies: THE 14 AUGUST AHDB/ECIU HARVEST DOWNGRADE WAS INSIDE THE PREVIOUS RUN'S WINDOW AND BOTH SWEEPS OF 16 AUGUST MISSED IT. ECIU published 'UK harvest even worse than previously thought' on 14 August, cutting the UK harvest to 18.5 Mt and raising the revenue loss to £550m. The runs of 16 August covered 10-16 August, checked ECIU by name, and recorded neither. It was recovered here only because FarmingUK wrote it up on 17 August. The pointer discipline worked as designed — a missed item inside a closed window is not re-swept — so this depended on luck, and a human may want to consider whether a source that publishes inside a window but is picked up late should trigger a look-back.

SEARCH RESULTS ARE SEVERELY CONTAMINATED BY 2025 AND 2023 ARTICLES THAT PRESENT AS CURRENT. Three candidate items were rejected on date after fetching: AgWeb's 'Indiana and Nebraska Crop Tour Numbers' (actually 19 August 2025, and the search engine's summary confidently attributed its Indiana 187.54 and Nebraska 173.25 figures to 2026), World Grain's 'Frost, dryness trim Australia's wheat outlook' (October 2024) and Grain Central's 'Canadian drought bites crop output hard' (September 2023). Every date in this run was verified from the page's own byline or metadata, never from the search result.

AN AGGREGATOR ON THE DROP LIST PUBLISHED WRONG NUMBERS FOR THE HEADLINE REPORT OF THE WEEK. indexbox.io, which badge_map already drops, carried the 17 August Crop Progress as corn 52% good to excellent 'down from 56%'. The correct figures are 60% and 61%, down one point each. The drop rule earned its keep.

US NATIONAL CONDITION SERIES ARE FRAGMENTING ACROSS FOUR SERIES KEYS AND A HUMAN SHOULD CONSOLIDATE. The same weekly national corn rating now sits under 'US|corn belt|maize|condition_good_excellent|DTN' (c005), 'US|corn belt and plains|...|DTN' (j018), 'US|midwest / corn belt|...|DTN' (a027) and, from this run, 'US|united states|maize|condition_good_excellent|USDA NASS' (u011). This run used region 'United States' and publisher 'USDA NASS' because that is what the formula gives for a national USDA figure, and STEP 5 forbids regenerating the earlier keys. The result is that a weekly national series with five readings available is spread over four one-reading series and will never chart.

TWO SCHEMA GAPS, BOTH NEW. There is no metric for a government support or subsidy payment (the £65m package, u003, filed under 'cost'), and none for soybean pod counts (u005, left unquantified). Pod counts recur every August during the Crop Tour and will be lost again next week without a metric.

A SERIES FORK ON THE UK REVENUE LOSS. a002 (-£390m) sits under publisher 'Farmers Weekly'; u002 (-£550m) sits under 'ECIU'. Both are the same ECIU estimate, revised. They cannot join without editing a002's key, which STEP 5 forbids. Flagged on the row and in the summary's conflicts.

FOURTEEN SERIES NOW HAVE MORE THAN ONE READING AND NO LABEL, up from thirteen. The new one is GB|united kingdom|mixed_grains|production|ECIU (19.5 then 18.5) — the single most quotable series in the corpus and it is off Tab 2 for want of one line of human text. Full list under series_needing_labels.

ARGENTINA AND INDIA: ZERO ROWS ACROSS THREE CONSECUTIVE RUNS. Argentina is carried in the manifest as a weekly-in-season source. India's FAS GAIN report has now failed to fetch on two separate runs with an empty body both times, which looks like a source-side problem rather than an absence of news.
REUTERS AND BLOOMBERG REMAIN UNREACHABLE by this agent, as reported on 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-16. Standing limitation.

NO ROW HAS AN EVENT_DATE MORE THAN A YEAR BEFORE ITS PUBLISHED_DATE. The largest gap in this run is 16 days (u006 to u009, USDA August forecasts with event_date 2026-08-01, published in the 17 August article).
NO KEY COLLISIONS AND NO SUFFIXING. The two unquantified rows took distinct fortnight keys (US|soybean|drought|yield|2026-08-B and US|maize|flood|yield|2026-08-B), separated by crop and hazard.
ZERO MERGES. All 18 claim_keys were free, so nothing this run duplicates the corpus.

ONLY TWO OF EIGHTEEN ROWS ARE POSITIVE (u009 Ohio soybeans, u018 US spring wheat), against the roughly one-in-five the design asks for. On a two-day window dominated by two negative reports this is not obviously a search failure, but it is worth watching.

VALIDATOR NOT RUN. STEP 8B forbids running any script in the repo, which includes validate.py. Its checks were reimplemented independently for this run's rows: flag_status/flag_note paired both ways, review_flag dual-written identically, every quantified row carrying event_date, series_key, metric_unit and a verbatim quote, every badge resolved against badge_map.json by the documented match rule, no duplicate ids, no claim_key collisions, and every shard compared field-for-field against all.json. All passed.

notes_on_judgement_calls: The national US condition rows cite Brownfield Ag News (Press, unmapped, appended to unmapped_domains.json) as the document read, because the USDA release itself never states a good-to-excellent figure — it publishes five separate condition columns, and adding good to excellent would be inferring a number, which the capture rules forbid. publisher and origin_publisher are set to USDA NASS so the series stays on the agency, following the DTN/USDA and Grain Central/GIWA precedents.
The USDA ESMIS Crop Progress text file was read first and its columns were used only as a check on Brownfield's prose, never as the source of a figure. They agree exactly.

The £65m package and the 18.5 Mt downgrade were both announced before window_start (15 and 14 August). Neither was taken under the never-checked exception, which does not apply here. They are recorded from in-window documents — FarmingUK of 17 August — with the out-of-window originals attached as corroborations, which is what the published_date rule permits.

The Pro Farmer Crop Tour was added to source_manifest.json with rhythm 'annual (August)'. It runs Monday to Thursday of one week each August and produced the only field-level US measurements of this window; a human should confirm the rhythm string.
month was set from published_date for all 18 rows, matching the dominant corpus convention and the runs of 16 August.
